instruction: Find the ChatGPT signup URL in the presentation and save it to a text file named "links.txt" on Desktop.

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting the ChatGPT signup URL from the presentation and saving it to a text file. Evaluator checks if 'https://chat.openai.com' is present in the output file. Verified by analyzing PPTX: slide 1 contains the URL 'https://chat.openai.com/' for signing up to ChatGPT.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: instruction asks for 'the ChatGPT signup URL' (singular, specific), and evaluator checks for exactly that URL
Getter logic is correct: reads text file from VM, extracts URLs using regex pattern, handles errors gracefully by returning empty list
Metric logic is correct: checks if expected URL 'https://chat.openai.com' is present in extracted URLs list using case-insensitive substring matching
Metric parameter handling is correct: directly accesses expected.get('url') for type='rule' (not expected.get('rules'))
Expected value is semantically correct: 'https://chat.openai.com' matches the ChatGPT signup URL from the presentation metadata
Data flow is correct: file content → URL extraction → presence verification
Substring matching handles trailing slash gracefully (expected 'https://chat.openai.com' matches actual 'https://chat.openai.com/' from presentation)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using exact URL matching instead of substring matching to avoid false positives (e.g., 'notahttps://chat.openai.com' would incorrectly match), though this is unlikely in practice
Consider normalizing URLs (strip trailing slashes, convert to lowercase) before comparison for more robust matching
